statements.impact_statement: Netty HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame validation bypass in codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport.

statements.status_notes: Netty verifyContinuationFrame fails to limit the number of zero-byte CONTINUATION frames, bypassing maxHeaderListSize and causing excessive CPU consumption on the server.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame flood DoS in Netty HTTP/2 codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound HTTP/2 listener.

Netty HTTP/2 codec vulnerability fixed in 4.1.133.Final / 4.2.13.Final. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no inbound HTTP/2 listener.

Netty HTTP/2 decompression ByteBuf reference-count leak in DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener, fixed in 4.1.136.Final / 4.2.16.Final. A remote peer can leak one direct ByteBuf per HTTP/2 DATA frame when a stream's decompressor has already been closed and the error path fails to release the retained buffer — but only in applications that run an HTTP/2 server with content decompression explicitly enabled via DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server and never enables HTTP/2 content decompression. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.
